 SCCH-23 3 MVC. No.6516/2023  JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m the deceased was traveling in a Toyota Qalis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 from Male Mahadeshwara Hill towards Bengaluru Side, on Kanakapura - Malavalli road and when reached near Kemmale Gate, NH-948 road, Malavalli Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that point of time the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 has driven from Kanakapura side towards Malavalli side, opposite direction with high speed, driven on extreme right side road in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed against the Toyota car, and dragged the car at a distance of 50 to 75 feet from the accident spot towards the car side road, in which the car was proceeding on correct side and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body and was succumbed to the fatal injuries on spot.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.

As the accident was caused by the reckless driving of the drivers of Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF- 8055 and KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

3. The respondent No.2 did not appear despite due service of notice of the petition upon him.
Hence he was placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.4 & 5 though entered appearance through their counsel, they failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
5. The respondent No.1/KSRTC Transport Corporation contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
It is alleged that the accident is occured due to the sole negligence of the driver of Qualis car in which the deceased was traveling.
The respondent corporation was no way responsible for the occurrence of accident.
This respondent denied the rash and negligent act of the driver of its bus driver.
On the contrary it is stated that on the date and time of alleged accident the bus in question was on its schedule trip from Kanakapura to Halaguru.

The driver of the KSRTC bus drive the same in slowly and cautiously on the extreme left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and while so proceeding on Kanakapura - Halaguru Main road, near Kemmale Gate at that point of time Qualis car
bearing

Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 came from the opposite side, being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with terrific speed in a zig-zag manner, observing the same the bus driver sensing some mishap, slowed down the speed of the bus and taken to its left side and when the things stood thus, car just like a bolt from the blue, came to its extreme right side of the road, by crossing the midpoint, the driver of the bus,
that too to extreme his right edge of the road, to avoid being hit by the car swear the bus to the little bit right side, but inspite of the same the driver of the car, due to the over speed and as the car moving in a zig zag manner totally lost control over the car and dashed violently against the bus and caused the accident, and due to the terrific hit by the car the bus moved to the right side.
As such, for the alleged accident the driver of the Qualis car was wholly and solely responsible, but the driver of bus in question was no way responsible.
However the petitioners with an oblique reasons foisted a false case in active collusion with the policy by creating a false crime records against this respondent driver.
Rest of the averments of the petition are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. The respondent No.3/Reliance General Insurance Company Limited appeared and filed written statement admitting the issuance of policy in respect of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 in favour of the respondent No.1 covering the alleged accident date, subject to the terms and conditions.
However negligence on the part of the driver of its insured car is denied.

Per contra it is alleged that the unfortunate accident occurred due to the rash & negligent act of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 came from Kanakapura side towards Malavalli side in opposite direction, driven on extreme its right side road and dashed to the car.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is submitted that the insured had knowingly entrusted his car to a driver who had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said class of vehicle.
Further the car was plied in a public place without having valid permit and fitness certificate.
On account of conscious breach of terms & conditions of the policy by the respondent No.1, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non -compliance of Sections 134(c) & 158(6) of IMV Act is pleaded.
Contending so prayed for dismissal of the petition.

3 7.
On the basis of above pleadings issues were framed.
However on 02.05.2025, issue No.1 was recasted as Additional Issue No.2 and certain additional issues were also framed.

They are reproduced as follows :
ISSUES Issue No.1 : Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m., near Kemmale gate, NH-948 road, Malavalli-Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli,
Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to actionable negligence of the drivers of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 and Toyota car bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MF- 8055 ?
Issue No.2 Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?

If so,
at what rate and from whom ?
Issue No.3 What order or award ?

ADDITIONAL ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she is the only legal representative of deceased 'and was dependent on him ?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m., near Kemmale gate, NH-948 road, Malavalli-Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to actionable negligence of the drivers of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 and Toyota car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 ?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?
If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
8. The Petitioner examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 11 were marked on behalf of the petitioner.
The petitioner has also examined the eye-witness to the accident as PW.2 and through her Ex.P.12 was marked.
The driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 was examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.3.
The Legal Claim Manager of the respondent No.3 was examined as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R1 & 2 documents.
9. Heard both counsels for the petitioner and respondents on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

10. My answers to the above issues are as follows:-

 REASONS 11. ADDITIONAL ISSUE No.1:
The petitioner claim that she is the wife of the deceased.
To prove the same, she filed affidavit-in-lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhaar cards of petitioner and deceased at Ex.P.10 & 11 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
During the course of her cross examination she stated that she don't have children.
She stated that the respondent No.4 and 5 and 5 are her mother-in-law and father- in-law.
They live in Neelathalli near Kunigal.
She stated that respondents No.4 and 5 were being looked after by other children, meaning everyone was looking after them together.
She further admitted that as per Ex.P.10 & 11 the address mentioned in the said documents are different.
She further admitted that they were different, he came every Friday and went to work on Monday.
She further stated that her deceased husband lived with her in Maddur.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioner with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioner is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimant, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner and respondents No.4 & 5 are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner and respondent No.4 and 5 are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to additional issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
12. ADDITIONAL ISSUE No.2:
The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of the complaint, the jurisdictional police registered a FIR against the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 and took up investigation.
During the course of investigation material evidence connected to the accident was collected by them.
There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place.
The death of the deceased person due to the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident is also not in conflict.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

The question as to who was responsible for the accident has to be answered by looking into the evidence on record,
perusal of which makes it evident that the Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 came and dashed against the front left side of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745, as a result of which the deceased and other inmates of the car succumbed on the spot.
This goes to show that the driver of the Qualis car had failed to adhere to the basic traffic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner.
The other tortfeasor i.e., driver of the KSRTC bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 (RW.1) who vehemently asserted that the said bus was express bus from Kanakapura to Halaguru.
He stated that the said road is NH-948 and the said road is straight road.
He further admitted that at the time of driving the vehicles were came opposite side could have been seen, he had seen the qualis car from 10 feet distance.
He further admitted that their was express bus, therefore there was a schedule to reach the destination.
The width of the road is 20 feet and accident took place at 4.30 p.m.

The learned counsel for petitioners put some questions to the driver of the KSRTC bus (RW.1) as :

sentences.text: "Question : Why you had taken the bus on right side on the road ?
Answer : The driver of the car came opposite side in zig zag manner, he came on left side of the road i.e on my side, so I had taken the bus on right side to avoid the accident".
RW.1 further admitted that the left front portion was damaged and has not produced photo of damaged bus.
He stated that he has not given any complaint as accident took place due to the negligence of the Qualis car, because he was also injured.

He stated that after 4 days from the date of accident he had taken bail from jurisdictional police and the criminal case is still pending at JMFC,
Kanakapura.
These elicitation make it amply clear that as RW.1 was driving his bus at a high speed and in a rash manner and bus dragged the car for certain distance.

A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the maximum, unfortunately has lead to death due to the careless act of RW.1.
13.
Smt. Bhagyalakshmi.
S (PW.2) filed affidavit evidence stating that she had eye-witnessed the accident.
She stated that she was traveling as passenger in an offending vehicle KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 from Kanakapura towards Halagur side.
The driver of the offending bus has driven with high speed and dashed against the Toyota car and after dragged the car at a distance of 50-75 feet from the accident spot.
The driver of the car was proceeding on correct side road and on proper lane from the opposite direction to an offending vehicle KSRTC bus.
During the course of her cross-examination, she admitted that she was sitting beside the driver seat on first seat.
She admitted that the road was busy road and the accident took place near the Kennare Gate.
She admitted that the bus which was proceeding at left side on the road, suddenly came towards right side and dashed to the car which was proceeding opposite to the bus on the left side.
She stated that if the bus driver had been drove the vehicle at his side, accident could have been avoided.
Nothing significant could be extracted from PW.2's mouth to disbelieve her presence at the spot of the accident, at the time of its occurrence.
14. Further on perusal of complaint given by one Shivalingegowda he being complainant witness in charge sheet.

He stated that on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m, one green Coloured Qualis car was coming from Halagur side with high speed in a zig zag manner and at the same time one KSRTC bus which was coming from Kanakapura side with high speed in rash and negligent manner and both have coming with high speed and themselves have caused the accident on head on collision.
He is third person.
He cannot be suspected that he is telling lie.
The complaint lodged by Shivalingegowda clearly shows that there was gross negligence of drivers of both vehicles.
As per the contents there was more negligence of driver of Qualis car.
From the testimonies of PW's.1 & 2 and complainant it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash & negligent driving of the both drivers.

Based on FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.8) against the drivers of KSRTC bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 and Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 for the offences punishable u/s's 279, 337, 338 and 304(A) of IPC.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the drivers of both car & KSRTC bus.
If driver of car had driven his car in his side and in normal speed, the accident could have been avoided.

Accordingly if KSRTC bus driver was driving the bus in Doddathyamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107215175/

15. Thus the unchallenged final report filed by the police clearly establishes negligence on the part of the drivers of the car and KSRTC bus.
A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the maximum, unfortunately has lead to injuries cased to the petitioner due to the careless act of drivers of both car and KSRTC bus.

The self serving statement of the driver of the KSRTC bus cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.

Be that as it may the inference that can be drawn from the police documents and evidence of PW.1 is that the driver of car and the driver of KSRTC bus were responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Thereby the negligence attributed towards driver of car and driver of KSRTC bus in the ratio of 70 :
30.

With this observation Issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
16. ADDITIONAL ISSUE NO.3 : LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:

The petitioner has produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P13 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 01.01.1971, which indicates that he was aged (52 years 7 months 27 days) 53 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '11'.
17.
In this case the claimants have claimed the compensation on the death of deceased in the RTA.

The petitioners contended that, deceased was working as Server at Legislative House Hotel,
Vidhanasoudha, Bengaluru and earning of Rs.30,000/-p.m.
However neither the avocation and income of the deceased is substantiated by producing cogent materials nor any witness is examined in this regard.
In the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 28.08.2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

Doddathyamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107215175/
7 18.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 53 years.
Therefore, in this case, 10% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 53 years and as such, 10% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.17,600/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/-
+ 1,600/- i.e. 10%).
19.
The deceased died living behind 3 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.11,733/- p.m. (Rs.17,600 - Rs.5,867 = Rs.11,733/-).
20. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,733/- p.m. and the multiplier '11' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.15,48,756/- (Rs.11,733/- X 12 X 11).

Considering the above facts,
I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,48,800/- under the head of loss of dependency.

21. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
By applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.

22. In this case, the respondent No.4 & 5 are the father and mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the respondent No.4 and 5 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father, as well as respondent No.4 and 5 towards deceased their son.
Therefore, respondent No.4 and 5 entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
25. Admittedly it is a case of composite negligence where injuries / death has been caused by a combined wrongful act of joint tortfeasors.

Under such circumstances, each wrong doer i.e., the respondents No.1 to 3 herein are jointly & severally liable and accordingly directed to pay the aforesaid award amount to the claimants together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondents No.1 & 3 being the insurers of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745 and car bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-MF-8055 are primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest in the ratio of 30 : 70, within one month from the date of this order.
As such, this issue is answered accordingly.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
26. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner and respondent No.4 and 5 are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,13,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondents No.1 & 3 are liable to pay and directed to deposit the aforesaid amount together with interest in the ratio of 30 : 70, within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
Due to the terrific impact the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over his body and was succumbed to the fatal injuries on spot.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
As the accident was caused by the reckless driving of the drivers of Qualis car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF- 8055 and KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-1745, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence he was placed exparte.
5. The respondent No.1/KSRTC Transport Corporation contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
On account of conscious breach of terms & conditions of the policy by the respondent No.1, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non -compliance of Sections 134(c) & 158(6) of IMV Act is pleaded.
opennyai_summary.issue:
They are reproduced as follows :
ISSUES Issue No.1 : Whether the petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m., near Kemmale gate, NH-948 road, Malavalli-Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli,
Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to actionable negligence of the drivers of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 and Toyota car bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MF- 8055 ?
Issue No.2 Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?
If so,
at what rate and from whom ?
Issue No.3 What order or award ?
ADDITIONAL ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she is the only legal representative of deceased 'and was dependent on him ?
2) Whether the petitioner proves that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 28.08.2023 at about 4.30 to 4.40 p.m., near Kemmale gate, NH-948 road, Malavalli-Kanakapura road, Sathanoor Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, due to actionable negligence of the drivers of KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1745 and Toyota car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-8055 ?
3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?
If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, petitioner and respondent No.4 and 5 are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
This Court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.3 & 4 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.8 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash and negligent act of the drivers of both car & KSRTC bus.
If driver of car had driven his car in his side and in normal speed, the accident could have been avoided.
15. Thus the unchallenged final report filed by the police clearly establishes negligence on the part of the drivers of the car and KSRTC bus.
A case of accident that would lead to grievous injuries at the maximum, unfortunately has lead to injuries cased to the petitioner due to the careless act of drivers of both car and KSRTC bus.
The self serving statement of the driver of the KSRTC bus cannot be attached any evidentiary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.
Be that as it may the inference that can be drawn from the police documents and evidence of PW.1 is that the driver of car and the driver of KSRTC bus were responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Thereby the negligence attributed towards driver of car and driver of KSRTC bus in the ratio of 70 :
30.
The petitioner has produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P13 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 01.01.1971, which indicates that he was aged (52 years 7 months 27 days) 53 years on the date of accident.
In this case the claimants have claimed the compensation on the death of deceased in the RTA.
However neither the avocation and income of the deceased is substantiated by producing cogent materials nor any witness is examined in this regard.
In the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
The deceased died living behind 3 dependents.
22. In this case, the respondent No.4 & 5 are the father and mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the respondent No.4 and 5 are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.
An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards his/her father, as well as respondent No.4 and 5 towards deceased their son.
. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
25. Admittedly it is a case of composite negligence where injuries / death has been caused by a combined wrongful act of joint tortfeasors.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above facts,
I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,48,800/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Therefore, respondent No.4 and 5 entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
Under such circumstances, each wrong doer i.e., the respondents No.1 to 3 herein are jointly & severally liable and accordingly directed to pay the aforesaid award amount to the claimants together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
As such, this issue is answered accordingly.
Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
26. ISSUE NO.4 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner and respondent No.4 and 5 are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,13,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondents No.1 & 3 are liable to pay and directed to deposit the aforesaid amount together with interest in the ratio of 30 : 70, within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Doddathyamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107215175/
9
Petitioner No.1 - 60% Respondent No.4 - 20% Respondent No.5 - 20%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
The entire share amount apportioned in the name of Respondent No.4 and 5 shall be released to in their favour through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
